title: Spawn raises its own alerts: the loop records each alert once per occurrence, with its evidence, and clears it with what cleared it; `spawn alerts` (once and follow) and the dashboard show the same ones, and the supervisor's hand-run monitor retires
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs, `resident_loop` (the steps of a pass, the disk watch that "never fails a pass", the failure count); crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs (the pattern this objective follows: a reading on a timer, one `host.disk` record per crossing of a threshold with a recovery margin so it does not flap, the latest records read back from the log on start so a restart records nothing twice); crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs and, in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql, `spawn_host_record`, `spawn_control_record`, `spawn_append_trusted`, the `host.disk` case of `spawn_control_apply` ("folded into no table") and its `else` (an unknown record type raises), the fold of `task.gated` (`gate_rejections`, `gate_aborts`, `gate_room_*`), `mission.halted` and `mission.resumed`; `halt_reason` and `HALT_AFTER` in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs (`step`'s loop over the workers, where "A managed worker between tasks is not news", `Why`, `Escalation::tag`) and dispatch/digest.rs; `LIKELY` in crates/spawn-core/src/observe/mod.rs, `Observation` (`stuck`, `attention`) in crates/spawn-core/src/observation.rs and the `observation.recorded` event; crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (attention); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (the routes, and `/api/scorecard`, an API that answers the CLI's own JSON); `USAGE`, `MORE_USAGE` and their tests in crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs; the supervisor's charter in crates/spawn-cli/src/supervise.rs (its Tools list); web/src (api.ts, App.tsx, Sidebar.tsx and the fleet view); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 (the digest), docs/storage.md ("Disk room"), docs/design.md §14; objective 023 (rsi/backlog/023.json: the loop's steps run when the event watermark moves or a timer is due, an idle minute costs at most 150 table scans) and the records objectives 028 (`execution.interrupted`, `execution.cleared`), 029 (`admission.waiting`, `admission.admitted`) 031 (`backup.dumped`, `backup.bundled` and their `over_alert`, `backup.verified`) and 033 (a `task.gated` host fault with `alert` true) define (rsi/backlog/028.json, 029.json, 031.json, 033.json).

The problem. Spawn has no alerts of its own. The supervisor runs a hand-written monitor (on this host /var/tmp/spawn/fleet-monitor.sh, a bash loop every 30 s, its rules restated here) that prints into its one pane: a task whose state changed (`TASK <id> -> <state> (mission, objective, agent)`, for missions 4, 6, 7 and 8 only); a mission whose state, halt, gate_rejections, gate_aborts or gate_room_escalated changed (`MISSION state changed: ...`); a task assigned for more than 5 minutes while its agent holds no delivered or reported task (`STUCK undelivered:<id>`); a command that finished failed, except the owner's notes (key `owner-note-...`); a line of the test or the live PostgreSQL container's log holding `terminated by signal`, `No space left` or `could not resize` (`docker logs --since`); MemAvailable under 4 GB (re-armed at 8 GB, the top three processes by RSS); and /tmp, a tmpfs in RAM, over 8,000 MB used (re-armed under 6,000; the three largest entries). It is the fleet's only alerting and nothing of it is recorded. Its state (`prev`, `seen`, `memlow`, `tmpfshigh`) lives in its process: after a restart it re-reports an undelivered task or low memory that is still true and never reports what changed while it was down; it needs docker, which neither the dashboard nor the gate's sandbox has; and what it says reaches only whoever reads that pane: no view of Spawn shows an alert, and no one can ask the record what went wrong overnight. Four conditions the owner wants told are not watched at all: an agent stuck by its latest judgement (objective 011's), an execution or a gate waiting for admission longer than a bound (029), a backup older than its schedule and a failed restore drill (031); and a model login that expired (028's `model_auth` wait) needs a person. Measured on the live main (b950e25) with rsi/scenarios/030.sh in BB_030_MEASURE=1 mode, five runs (two on b950e25, three on 13668eb, the deploy before it, with the same behaviour), and a sixth on b950e25 with the two records 031 and 033 now write (2026-11-06 18:25 CST: neither shown anywhere): of the 17 conditions the scenario provokes, Spawn records none and shows one: the halt reaches the supervisor's digest as a `halted` stall 155-234 ms after `mission.halted` (SPAWN_STALL_HALTED_SECS 0). A resident judged stuck (0.9) between tasks gets `spawn fleet` attention 1.7-1.8 s after its turn but never reaches the digest (dispatch.rs skips a managed worker between tasks); the task changes, the failed command, the crash lines, memory, /tmp, the undelivered task (its delivery stall is 600 s), the admission wait, the backups, the drill and the model login show nowhere; `GET /api/alerts` answers 404. On this host now: /tmp 3,838 of 16,017 MiB used, MemAvailable 19.9 GiB (2026-11-06 17:20 CST, 09:20 UTC).

Owner ruling (2026-11-06). The supervisor's charter may name `spawn alerts`: (5) stands. The PostgreSQL log settings (SPAWN_DATABASE_LOG, SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG) and the containers' log files are owner work through deploy/, not part of what an agent implements for this objective: the candidate reads a log when its setting names one, and says once that it reads none otherwise; making the two containers write log files and naming them in spawn.env is the owner's (see the precondition below). In the owner's order this objective comes after 028, 033 (with 020), 031 and 029, so two alerts the owner ruled for those objectives exist before it as fields of their producers' records, and become alerts here: objective 033's, a `task.gated` host fault with `alert` true (the third base in a row on a mission that disagreed with itself, which until now the dispatcher's digest takes to the supervisor), and objective 031's, a `backup.dumped` or `backup.bundled` with `over_alert` true (R2 holds more than its alert threshold, 8 GB).

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. The record. Each alert transition is a control record the loop writes through the owner's store (a new owner-only `spawn_alert_record`, as `spawn_host_record` writes `host.disk`): `{"type": "alert.fired", "key", "kind", "subject", "evidence": {...}, "text"}` and `{"type": "alert.cleared", "key", "kind", "subject", "evidence": {...}}`; a notice is an `alert.fired` with `"notice": true` and never clears. `key` names the occurrence (below). The store folds them into a table of alerts keyed by `key` and refuses a second `alert.fired` for a key, an `alert.cleared` without its `alert.fired`, and a second `alert.cleared`: an alert fires once per occurrence and clears at most once, across loop restarts and two loops at once. Every record-borne alert names in `evidence.event_id` the record that started it, and its clearing names in `evidence.event_id` the record that cleared it. Evidence never holds a secret: no database URL with its password, no environment, process names without their arguments. `text` is one line for a person.
2. The kinds (`kind`, `subject`, `key`, when it fires, when it clears, the evidence):
Notices, the monitor's change lines, for every mission:
- `task_state`, `task #<id>`, `task_state:<task id>:<event id>`: each control record after which the task's state differs from before it (its `task.assigned`: from none); evidence `task`, `mission`, `objective`, `agent_id`, `from`, `to`, `record` (its type), `event_id`. A record that leaves the state as it was (an `aborted` or `stale` gating) is no notice.
- `mission_state`, `mission #<id>`, `mission_state:<mission id>:<event id>`: each control record after which any of the mission's `state`, `halted`, `gate_rejections`, `gate_aborts`, `gate_room_escalated` differs from before; evidence `mission`, `record`, `event_id`, `before` and `after` (those five).
- `gate_base_disagrees`, `mission #<id>`, `gate_base_disagrees:<event id of the task.gated>`: a `task.gated` record with verdict `host_fault`, evidence `base_disagrees` and `alert` true (objective 033: the third base in a row on the mission that disagreed with itself; written by the integrator, not by this objective, and before this objective exists that record is the alert); evidence `task`, `mission`, `scenario`, `exits`, `base_disagrees`, `setup_s` (when the record has it), `due_ms`, `event_id`.
- `command_failed`, `command #<id>`, `command_failed:<command id>`: a command finished with `succeeded` false, except an owner note (idempotency key `owner-note-...`); evidence `command`, `agent_id`, `session_id`, `principal`, `action` (its type), `key`, `error` (its first 300 characters).
Conditions:
- `task_undelivered`, `task #<id>`, `task_undelivered:<task id>:<event id of its task.assigned>`: in state `assigned` longer than SPAWN_ALERT_UNDELIVERED_SECS (default 300, the monitor's 5 minutes) while its agent holds no `delivered` or `reported` task; clears when it leaves `assigned` (the record that moved it).
- `mission_halted`, `mission #<id>`, `mission_halted:<mission id>:<event id of mission.halted>`: evidence `reason`, `gate_rejections`, `gate_aborts`, `event_id`; clears at its `mission.resumed`.
- `postgres_crash`, `test` (the log SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG names, objective 020's setting) or `live` (SPAWN_DATABASE_LOG, new), `postgres_crash:<subject>:<the first matching line's stamp and [pid], as written>`: a line holding `terminated by signal`, `No space left` or `could not resize` (the monitor's patterns), stamped within the last day (`%m [%p] `, UTC or a numeric offset, as 020 reads it); evidence `log` (the path) and `lines` (that occurrence's matching lines, at most 10); clears at the first `database system is ready to accept connections` line after them (evidence `line`), or when SPAWN_ALERT_PG_QUIET_SECS (default 900) pass with no matching line (evidence `quiet_secs`, `last_line`). The loop reads each log on the host timer, only the bytes appended since its last read (on start, the last MiB); a log unset or unreadable is no reading, said once in the loop's output.
- `memory_low`, `host`, `memory_low:<ms of the reading>`: MemAvailable of /proc/meminfo, in MiB, under SPAWN_ALERT_MEMORY_LOW_MB (default 4096, the monitor's 4 GB); clears at or above SPAWN_ALERT_MEMORY_OK_MB (default 8192, where the monitor re-arms). Evidence `measured_mb`, `threshold_mb` and `top` (the three largest processes by RSS: `pid`, `rss_mb`, `name`, the command name only); the clearing `measured_mb`, `threshold_mb`.
- `tmpfs_high`, `host`, `tmpfs_high:<ms of the reading>`: the used MiB of the filesystem holding SPAWN_ALERT_TMPFS_PATH (default /tmp) over SPAWN_ALERT_TMPFS_HIGH_MB (default 8000, the monitor's); clears under SPAWN_ALERT_TMPFS_OK_MB (default 6000). Evidence `path`, `measured_mb`, `threshold_mb`.
Both host readings, and the logs, are taken every SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS (default 30, the monitor's period). A threshold of 0 disables its check; one that does not parse is said once and its default used.
- `agent_stuck`, the session id, `agent_stuck:<session>:<event id of the observation>`: the session's latest `observation.recorded` (which, per objective 011, covers its latest fact) says `stuck` at or above LIKELY (0.5, the Observer's own attention threshold), for every session, whatever the dispatcher does with it; evidence `agent_id`, `stuck`, `state`, `judge`, `event_id`; a later observation still stuck fires nothing; clears when the latest observation says `stuck` under 0.5 (evidence `stuck`, `event_id`) or its execution ended by a stop.
- `admission_wait`, the record's `agent_id` (an execution) or `task #<id>` (a gate), `admission_wait:<event id of admission.waiting>`: an `admission.waiting` (029) with no `admission.admitted` of the same `kind` and `agent_id` or `task` after it, older than SPAWN_ALERT_ADMISSION_SECS (default 600: an agent that cannot start is down, and ten minutes is a third of one gate's run on 2026-11-06, 1,417-1,917 s); evidence `kind`, `envelope_bytes`, `measure`, `measured_bytes`, `threshold_bytes`, `event_id`; clears at that `admission.admitted` (evidence `waited_ms`, `event_id`).
- `backup_stale`, `dump` or `bundle`, `backup_stale:<subject>:<event id of the newest backup.dumped or backup.bundled>`: the newest such record older than SPAWN_ALERT_BACKUP_DUMP_MAX_AGE_SECS (default 7200: the hourly dump's schedule twice, so one late run is not told and a missed one is) or SPAWN_ALERT_BACKUP_BUNDLE_MAX_AGE_SECS (default 93600: the daily bundle's day plus two hours); with no such record at all there is no alert (that fleet has no backups set up, as every scenario's database); evidence `key` (the object), `age_secs`, `max_age_secs`, `event_id`; clears at a newer record (evidence `key`, `event_id`); that record growing old is a new occurrence.
- `backup_budget`, `r2`, `backup_budget:<event id of the record>`: a `backup.dumped` or `backup.bundled` (031) with `over_alert` true (R2 holds, with that run's copies, more than SPAWN_BACKUP_R2_ALERT_MB, 8 GB by default: the owner's alert on the way to the free tier's 10 GB, which 031 never writes past) while no `backup_budget` alert is open; evidence `held_bytes`, `written_bytes`, `alert_bytes`, `limit_bytes`, `skipped`, `event_id`; clears at the first later `backup.dumped` or `backup.bundled` with `over_alert` false (evidence `held_bytes`, `event_id`). Before this objective exists the record is the alert (031).
- `drill_failed`, `drill`, `drill_failed:<event id>`: a `backup.verified` with `ok` false; evidence `key`, `reason`, `events`, `max_event_id`, `expected`, `event_id`; clears at the next `backup.verified` with `ok` true.
- `model_auth`, the session id, `model_auth:<event id of execution.interrupted>`: an `execution.interrupted` (028) with cause `model_auth`: a person must log the engine in again; evidence `agent_id`, `execution_id`, the record's `evidence`, `event_id`; clears at that execution's `execution.cleared` (evidence `waited_ms`, `event_id`).
These records of 028, 029, 031 and 033 are read from the log (spawn_events), never from a table their producers may fold them into, and no record type or verdict this objective does not fold is refused by it: the scenario appends them as their producers write them (spawn_append_trusted, no fold), so this objective can be solved before 028, 029, 031 and 033.
3. When (the number this objective states). A record-borne alert (a notice, a halt, a stuck judgement, a model login, a failed drill, a clearing) is recorded within one loop pass of its record: within 1 s at the default 500 ms interval (the scenario's bound: 5 s); a host reading or a log line within SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS and one pass (30 s and a pass; the monitor's 30 s, but recorded); a bound (an undelivered task, an admission wait, a backup's age) within one pass of falling due, never before, measured from its record's `recorded_at_ms` by the database's clock. Alerts per occurrence: exactly one `alert.fired`, at most one `alert.cleared`, whatever restarts. The step keeps objective 023's rule: it runs when the event watermark moved or one of its timers is due (the next host reading, the earliest bound that falls due), keeps the open alerts in memory after reading them once, and adds no table scan to an idle minute in which no alert changes (023's IDLE_MAX, 150, holds). Like the disk watch it never fails a pass: an error is said and tried at the next check.
4. The same alerts everywhere. `spawn alerts --once [--json] [--since <duration or ms>]` prints every open alert and every alert fired or cleared within the window (default SPAWN_ALERT_WINDOW_SECS, 86400), in the order fired: with `--json` one JSON array of `{"key", "kind", "subject", "state" ("open", "cleared" or "notice"), "fired_event_id", "fired_at_ms", "evidence", "cleared_event_id", "cleared_at_ms", "cleared_evidence", "text"}` (the cleared fields null while open), without it one line per alert naming its state, kind, subject, time and text; exit 0, with none too. `spawn alerts --follow [--json] [--since <event id>]` prints each transition recorded after it starts (or after that event) as it is recorded, one line each, flushed per line (`{"transition": "fired" or "cleared", "key", "kind", "subject", "event_id", "at_ms", "evidence", "notice"}` with `--json`), and runs until it is stopped. `GET /api/alerts` (and `?since=`) answers the same JSON array as `spawn alerts --once --json`, from the same store method, as `/api/scorecard` answers the CLI's scorecard. The dashboard (web/src) shows the open alerts on every page (kind, subject, since when, text) and an Alerts view with the window's alerts, their evidence and their clearing. MORE_USAGE names `spawn alerts`; the contract's USAGE line stays as it is.
5. The monitor retires. The supervisor's charter names `spawn alerts --follow` and `spawn alerts --once` in its Tools list, in place of any monitor of its own.
6. Causality (§14): an alert rests on a named record (its event id) or a recorded reading (its measure and threshold, in its evidence); a clearing names what cleared it; nothing rests on a process's memory (a restarted loop reads its alerts back and fires nothing twice), on absence (no backup record means no alert, never "no backup"), or on time without a record.
None of the other objectives' scenarios may regress: alert records are written only on transitions, in the pass that sees their cause; 023's idle bound holds; no session gets a fact from an alert (011's (3)); every scenario that counts control records counts them by type.

How the saving shows, in numbers. Today, of the 17 conditions the scenario provokes, Spawn records 0 and shows 1 (the halt, as a stall digest, 0.16-0.23 s after it); the monitor polls every 30 s, writes to one pane, re-reports after a restart what is still true and loses what changed while it was down. With this objective: 17 of 17 recorded with their evidence, each once, a record-borne one within a pass (1 s) of its record and a reading within 30 s and a pass, each cleared with what cleared it, and the same in `spawn alerts`, its stream and the dashboard. On 017's scorecard it shows as autonomy and reliability: a halted mission, a stuck agent, a dead login or a stale backup is told by the record, not by whoever watches a pane.

State the rule in the module comment of a new crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the kinds, keys, thresholds and the once-per-occurrence rule), in docs/fleet-architecture.md (an "Alerts" section beside §3's digest), in docs/storage.md (the records and the table) and in schema.sql beside the fold. Add unit tests: each kind's firing and clearing as a pure function of records and readings; the hysteresis of memory (4096/8192) and /tmp (8000/6000) with no flapping between; the keys; a restart (the alerts read back) fires nothing twice; notices from task and mission records (from and to, before and after; none for an `aborted` gating); `command_failed` skipping owner notes; the crash-line parser (the three patterns, the ready line, the quiet clearing, UTC and offset stamps); evidence holding no URL password with one in the environment; the backup ages (none without a record, a newer record clears, its age a new occurrence); `backup_budget` fired by `over_alert` once per crossing and cleared by a record under it; `gate_base_disagrees` from a host fault with `alert` true and none from one without it; the admission pairing; the CLI's JSON and text and `/api/alerts` giving the same array; the charter naming `spawn alerts`. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: the fold of `alert.fired` and `alert.cleared` and its three refusals, and `spawn_alert_record` refused to any login but the owner's.

Precondition the owner provides (deploy/, not this objective's candidate; the owner's ruling of 2026-11-06): the live and test PostgreSQL servers run in docker containers (spawn-rsi-pg, spawn-test-pg) whose logs only docker reads; until the owner makes each write a log file the loop can read and names them in spawn.env (SPAWN_DATABASE_LOG, SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG), the crash alert reads no log and says so once. The scenario needs neither.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/030.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). A real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, the dispatcher, the supervisor) runs a resident `r1` of one gated mission and the supervisor on a fake engine, with a fake model judge (SPAWN_JUDGE_URL, a loopback server answering WAITING, needs_human 0.3, and stuck 0.9 for the sessions it is told, else 0.05); `spawn serve` answers on a loopback port and `spawn alerts --follow --json` runs from the start; the loop runs with SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS=2, SPAWN_ALERT_UNDELIVERED_SECS=3, SPAWN_ALERT_ADMISSION_SECS=3, both backup ages 4 s, two log files of its own and host thresholds that never fire, except while it is restarted with thresholds the host crosses. It checks:
- (1) `spawn alerts --once --json` exits 0 with a JSON array, `GET /api/alerts` answers 200 with one, and `--follow --json` keeps running;
- (2) T1 (r1) goes assigned, delivered, reported: one `task_state` notice per record (key, `to`, `event_id`), each within 5 s of its record;
- (3) an input to a session with no execution fails: one `command_failed` notice (key `command_failed:<id>`, the error) within 5 s;
- (4) a gate that aborts three passes in a row halts the mission: one `mission_state` notice per aborted gating (record `task.gated`, after.gate_aborts 1, 2, 3), one `mission_halted` alert within 5 s (key, `reason`), shown by the text form too; `spawn mission resume` clears it, naming the `mission.resumed` record;
- (5) crash lines appended to both logs: one `postgres_crash` alert each (`test`, `live`) within 10 s, none again on later readings; a ready line clears each, quoted;
- (6) restarted with thresholds the host crosses and SPAWN_DISK_FLOOR_GB holding new executions: one `memory_low` and one `tmpfs_high` within 20 s (measure and threshold, the path); T2, assigned to a new worker that cannot start, one `task_undelivered` 3-8 s after its `task.assigned`; restarted as usual, the three clear (T2's naming its `task.delivered`) and nothing fires twice;
- (7) r1 judged stuck after a turn: one `agent_stuck` within 5 s of that observation; another stuck turn fires nothing; judged not stuck after a third, it clears;
- (8) appended records: `admission.waiting` gives one `admission_wait` 3-8 s after it, cleared by its `admission.admitted`; `backup.dumped` and `backup.bundled` one `backup_stale` each 4-9 s after them, cleared by newer ones; `backup.verified` ok false one `drill_failed` within 5 s, cleared by one ok true; `execution.interrupted` cause `model_auth` one `model_auth` within 5 s, cleared by its `execution.cleared`; a `task.gated` host fault with `alert` true (033's) one `gate_base_disagrees` notice within 5 s; a `backup.dumped` with `over_alert` true one `backup_budget` within 5 s, cleared by one with `over_alert` false;
- (9) every one of those alerts once, with the same state and event ids, in `spawn alerts --once --json`, `GET /api/alerts` and the `--follow` stream (one `fired` line, and one `cleared` after it for a condition); the log holds no alert transition twice.
On the live main (b950e25; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1), in 1-2 s: "(1) `spawn alerts --once --json` exited 1 (spawn: unknown command alerts): Spawn raises no alerts of its own; today the supervisor's hand-run monitor (fleet-monitor.sh) prints them in one pane, unrecorded". With BB_030_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it goes on for 118-147 s and every check fails (`GET /api/alerts` answers 404; the follow mode exits at once); of the provoked conditions only the halt reaches the supervisor's digest (a `halted` stall, 155-362 ms after its record), the stuck judgement (recorded 1.7-1.8 s after the turn) sets `spawn fleet` attention and no digest, and nothing shows the rest. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
